title: A flat finitely presented morphism has a locally quasi-finite neighbourhood over every image point
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], and let $s\in S$ be a point in the image of $f$. Then there exist a scheme $S'$ and morphisms $h:S'\to X$ and $g:S'\to S$ with $g=f\circ h$ and $s\in g(S')$, such that $g$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], and locally quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite].

proof.text: Because $s$ lies in the image of $f$, the fibre $X_s$ is nonempty. Locally finite presentation implies locally finite type: the images of the finitely many polynomial variables generate each affine presentation algebra. Apply [lem-sbc-composite-fibre-local-models] with $a=\mathrm{id}_X$ and the given $f$. Its affine fibre neighbourhoods show that $X_s$ is locally of finite type over $\kappa(s)$, and its stalk assertion shows that every local ring of $X_s$ is Noetherian. Let $C_s$ be the locus in $X_s$ where depth equals Krull dimension. By this Noetherianity, $C_s$ is exactly the Cohen–Macaulay locus of [lem-trf-flat-lfp-cm-locus-fibre-dense], hence is dense and nonempty. By [lem-sbc-fibre-cohen-macaulay-locus-open], it is also open: it is the inverse image of that node's open locus under the fibre projection. Apply [lem-sc-lft-over-field-jacobson-space] with the closed subset equal to all of $X_s$. Its density of closed points implies that the nonempty open $C_s$ contains a point $x$ closed in $X_s$. This $x$ has a Noetherian Cohen–Macaulay fibre local ring, as required for the slice lemma.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-cm-closed-point-flat-quasifinite-slice] to $f$, $s$, and the closed Cohen–Macaulay point $x$. It gives a scheme $S'$, a morphism $h:S'\to X$, and a point $z\in S'_s$ with $h(z)=x$, such that the composite $g=f\circ h$ is flat, locally of finite presentation, and locally quasi-finite.

proof.text: By construction $g=f\circ h$, and $s=g(z)$ because $z\in S'_s$. Thus $s\in g(S')$, and all the asserted properties of $g$ hold.
